brief.recommendation: Checkout success is 80% (BIZ-3) vs 95% SLO, with $3,714/min revenue at risk. Waiting 592s (BIZ-4) costs ~$36,624 and EXCEEDS the 60s tolerance. Termination is vetoed by MEMORY (previously ineffective) and lacks required biz.change_calendar evidence (I2). Neither waiting nor terminating is acceptable; escalation to the pricing team owner is required.

audit.report: The batch_replayable_price_sync job (pid 158987) entered an idle transaction that blocked checkout sessions, degrading success from 95% SLO to 80% and putting approximately $3,714/min of revenue at risk. After 52.8 seconds of negotiation, both guardians rejected waiting (which would exceed the 60-second business degradation tolerance with ~592s remaining runtime) and terminating (which was previously verified ineffective and lacks required change-calendar evidence). The case was escalated to the pricing team for human decision.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_price_sync process became idle in transaction with an open txn lasting >8s, blocking checkout sessions and violating the 60-second degradation tolerance.
lessons: Check biz.change_calendar before proposing termination: batch_replayable_price_sync has no active change-calendar window, so terminating it violates policy I2 and risks MEMORY veto.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians correctly rejected waiting and terminating based on the evidence, but the negotiation consumed 2 full rounds before escalating; the database_guardian did not probe biz.change_calendar or db.lock_graph until after the Continuity Guardian's first rejection, wasting time.
follow_ups: Add a 60-second waiting limit with automatic escalation for batch_replayable_price_sync in future negotiations.
Require biz.change_calendar check as a precondition for any terminate proposal on batch jobs.
Log lock-graph snapshots at incident start to provide immediate root-blocker context to both guardians.
